Description: Around the start of dinner, many people gather in the Dining room and, for the first time publicly, bring up the death in the Study—triggering tense confrontation and multiple branching character movements.
Location: Dining room（Dining room）
Key Information:
  - Dinner is about to begin; Martha Galley takes charge of Dining room order and arranges seating.
  - A conversation between Helen Dauer and Annie Beaumont hints Annie may have seen the deceased earlier, but Annie denies it and says she didn’t see clearly.
  - Damian Maseko helps Martha Galley retrieve dishes from the dumbwaiter, confirming dinner preparations continue.
  - Helen Dauer mentions again that her daughter is not present; Damian Maseko guesses she is sleeping.
  - At the table, Edmund Galley formally challenges John Hobbes’s identity for the first time and questions why he is at dinner.
  - Damian Maseko publicly reveals: earlier, an unidentified person was found dead in the Study, and the matter had originally been handled in secret.
  - Annie Beaumont says she may have seen the dead person before, drawing attention from those present.
  - Tony Dauer explicitly rules out the dead person being Oswald, saying he has just seen him.
  - John Hobbes states publicly: the dead person is the same individual who invited him here—Rupert Galley.
  - Edmund Galley reacts with strong confusion and anger to the name “Rupert Galley,” indicating he does not know this person.
  - After thunder, a sound of plates breaking comes from the Kitchen directly beneath the Dining room, interrupting the discussion and prompting urgent reactions.
  - Edmund Galley orders John Hobbes to leave the Dining room with him for a private talk.
  - Martha Galley says she needs to find Oswald because his dinner has not been served.
  - Despite Annie Beaumont calling out to him, Tony Dauer leaves, saying he needs to fetch something.
  - Damian Maseko notes that Eve Dauer is in Edmund Galley’s room, hinting Tony Dauer’s destination may relate to that.
  - Apart from those who left, the remaining people stay in the Dining room awaiting developments.
Characters:
  [John Hobbes（John Hobbes）] Person No. 1, a visitor.
    · Is required to confirm his identity again at the table.
    · Publicly states the dead person is Rupert Galley, the one who invited him.
    · Is ordered by Edmund Galley to leave the Dining room for a private talk.
  [Martha Galley（Martha Galley）] Person No. 5, the lady of the villa.
    · Leads dinner arrangements and maintains order.
    · Defends John Hobbes when he is questioned, stressing he is unrelated to the death.
    · Leaves the Dining room after the Kitchen noise to look for Oswald.
  [Edmund Galley（Edmund Galley）] Person No. 6, one of the villa’s hosts.
    · Shows displeasure and vigilance about John Hobbes being at dinner.
    · Reacts intensely to the name Rupert Galley, insisting he does not know him.
    · Acts immediately after the Kitchen noise, taking John Hobbes out of the Dining room.
  [Damian Maseko（Damian Maseko）] Person No. 8.
    · Helps prepare dinner and keep the process moving.
    · Is the first to publicly disclose the Study death at the table.
    · States Eve Dauer is currently in Edmund Galley’s room.
  [Helen Dauer（Helen Dauer）] Person No. 9.
    · Closely watches Annie Beaumont’s reactions.
    · Expresses strong dissatisfaction and suspicion about the coincidence of a stranger and a death.
  [Annie Beaumont（Annie Beaumont）] Person No. 2.
    · Denies clearly seeing the dead person but implies she may have seen them earlier.
    · Tries to stop Tony Dauer when he prepares to leave.
  [Tony Dauer（Tony Dauer）] Person No. 4.
    · Explicitly rules out the dead person being Oswald.
    · Leaves again after a brief stay in the Dining room, saying he needs to get something.
  [Victoria Maseko（Victoria）] Person No. 7.
    · Pays close attention to the tense interaction between Tony Dauer and Annie Beaumont at the table.
